description: Constant-power-style two-file mixer with a single complementary fader: output = balance*file1 + (1-balance)*file2 (verified exactly: default renders 0.5/0.5; -k0.7 renders 0.7000/0.3000 by least-squares gain recovery). Because the two gains always sum to 1, the mix is a convex combination and CANNOT overload - like merge, the safe counterpart to submix mix's wraparound. balance is TIME-VARIABLE (banner-confirmed 'Balance may vary over time' and breakpoint-verified: a 0->1 ramp renders distinct from BOTH the k=0 and k=1 scalar renders). Output duration = INDUR1 exactly, both orders probed (1s+2s -> 1.0; 2s+1s -> 2.0): if file 2 is shorter the output continues as balance*file1 alone; if longer, its tail past indur1 is discarded. begin/end crop the mix (output = end - begin when both set, verified 1.0 from -b0.5 -e1.5). Inputs MUST share one channel count in practice - see known_issues for the mixed-channel corruption. Deterministic.
musical_use: The single-knob crossfader: automate balance with a breakpoint envelope to duck one layer under another, ride a drone against a texture, or hand-shape a slow transition with an arbitrary contour (where submix crossfade is a single fixed-shape fade, balance takes any trajectory - dip to 0.2 and come back, oscillate, step). balance 1 = all file 1, 0 = all file 2, 0.5 = equal halves. Since the envelope's time axis runs over file 1's duration (= the output), design gestures in file-1 time. Convexity means you can balance two full-scale sources fearlessly - no getlevel pre-flight needed. For weighted static sums where the gains should NOT sum to 1, use submix mix with explicit levels; for a one-way transition with a perceptually-tuned curve, submix crossfade mode 2's powfac skew.

balance.description: File 1's gain; file 2 gets (1 - balance). CDP-enforced 0-1 ('-k1.5' refused verbatim). BREAKPOINT-CAPABLE (verified: 0->1 ramp differs from both scalar-endpoint renders); envelope axis = file 1's duration = the output duration. CDP default 0.5 (equal mix, verified).

begin.description: Start the mix at this time. CDP-enforced 0 to INDUR1 (input-dependent: refusal on a 1 s file quotes '(0.000000 to 1.000000)'). Breakpoint refused (parameter 2). Omitted unless set.

end.description: Stop the mix at this time (same 0-to-INDUR1 bound as begin, quoted verbatim on refusal). With begin set, output duration = end - begin (verified). Breakpoint refused (parameter 3). Omitted unless set.

examples.description: Duck a texture under a foreground gesture, then let it back up.
examples.expected_use: input = [foreground, texture]. Relative times compile against file 1's duration. Gains stay complementary throughout - no overload possible.
Output = 0.7*file1 + 0.3*file2, lasting exactly as long as file 1.

known_issues: MIXED CHANNEL COUNTS PRODUCE CORRUPT OUTPUT (first-class divergence): the banner says 'files may or may not have different number of channels', but the binary neither converts nor refuses - a 2 s mono + 1 s stereo pair rendered a FOUR-second mono file of channel-interleave garbage (content matches neither source; no INFO/ERROR printed). Only equal channel counts verified clean (mono+mono, stereo+stereo). Match channels yourself (housekeep chans / submix interleave) before calling.
Output duration = INDUR1 always: file 2 shorter -> the remainder is balance*file1 alone (file 2 falls silent); file 2 longer -> its tail is DISCARDED. Put the file whose full length you want first.

Overload-safe by construction: gains are complementary (sum 1), verified at multiple balance values - two full-scale inputs cannot exceed full scale. Contrast submix mix (WRAPS) and submix faders (wraps via its overall envelope).
Sample rates must match: 'ERROR: INCORRECT USE / ERROR: Different sample-rates in input files: can't proceed.' (exit 255).
begin/end refuse breakpoints (parameters 2-3); balance is the only time-variable parameter. Deterministic: identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart.

Multi-input entry: duration rule (indur1; end-begin under cropping) verified in docs/curation/tranche12_submix_depth.md; incompatible with the single-input duration fixture (duration_row null, tranche-11 rule).
